Where it began

Litton Das was born in Dinajpur in 1994. He was picked for the national Under-15 side at just 13, went on to study and play at the Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protishtan, and went to the Under-19 World Cup twice, in 2012 and again in 2014.

His first big domestic season was a remarkable one. Rangpur Division had him for the 2014–15 National Cricket League, and he made 1,024 runs in seven matches at 85.33, with five hundreds, and Rangpur took the title. A few seasons later he made 274 in a single innings in the Bangladesh Cricket League.

The player

He made his Test debut against India in June 2015, and in 2017 he was handed the gloves for a Test series against Sri Lanka. His first Test hundred was a while coming. He fell five short against Zimbabwe in 2021 before finally getting there against Pakistan that November. After that they came more readily. In January 2022 his 86 helped Bangladesh to their first Test win in New Zealand, at Bay Oval, and in May that year he made 141 against Sri Lanka.

By November 2026 he had played 58 Tests, scoring 3,549 runs at 36.21 with seven hundreds and 21 fifties. Behind the stumps he had held 126 catches and made 19 stumpings. In 2024 he took 12 dismissals in a two-Test series against Pakistan, more than any Bangladeshi keeper had managed in a series, and made 138 in the same series to be named man of the match.

What made him special

He could score very quickly when the game called for it. In an ODI against Zimbabwe in 2020 he made 176, at the time the highest score by a Bangladeshi in the format, and shared a stand of 292 with Tamim Iqbal. In 2023 he reached fifty in 18 balls in a T20 international against Ireland, the fastest by a Bangladeshi at that point.

Coming in at six or lower, he four times scored both a hundred and a half-century in one Test. In one Test he paired that double with nine dismissals behind the stumps, which nobody had done before him. As a bowler he had less to show: he did turn his arm over in Tests, but the wicket column stayed politely blank.

In charge

He was named Test vice-captain in 2022, and when he stood in for Shakib Al Hasan he became Bangladesh's 12th Test captain. They won that match by their biggest margin in runs. He led the ODI side to a 2–1 series win over India in December 2022, and in December 2024 his T20 side won all three matches in the West Indies. In May 2025 he was made T20 captain through to the 2026 World Cup.

In franchise cricket he helped Comilla Victorians to back-to-back Bangladesh Premier League titles, and he also turned out for Jamaica Tallawahs and Kolkata Knight Riders.

And finally

One Test as captain, one win, and a record margin besides. By November 2026 his record in charge of the Test side was perfect, which is more than most captains can say.
